purpose: Named product-level examples in which a regulator-authored or regulator-hosted source documents material use of a NAM in regulatory decision-making. This dataset is broader than animal-study displacement: every record explicitly states what evidence was displaced or supplemented, and records that did not replace animal studies must not be counted as animal displacement.

cases.indication: HLA-A*02:01-positive unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma
cases.nam: Human tissue and cell-based in vitro assays assessing target/species specificity, cross-reactivity in 35 human tissues, organ-specific toxicity potential in 13 tissues, cytokines and cytolytic proteins
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported the safety of clinical trials in the absence of a pharmacologically relevant animal model and contributed to development leading to approval.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Pharmacologically relevant animal model was unavailable; the human in vitro assay suite supplied nonclinical safety and mechanistic evidence needed to support clinical development.
cases.cross_jurisdiction_note: EMA product information states that tebentafusp is human-specific and that there are no relevant animal species in which its nonclinical toxicology could be tested. TGA's AusPAR independently states that the absence of animal-species toxicity studies was justified by human specificity and absence of equivalent targets, while describing the supporting human target-binding, tissue-panel, cytokine and related in vitro evidence. This makes Kimmtrak a cross-jurisdiction precedent rather than an FDA-only anecdote.
cases.note: FDA/CDER/OND authors explicitly identify Kimmtrak as a NAM regulatory-decision example and state that the human tissue/cell assay suite supported clinical-trial safety in the absence of pharmacologically relevant animal models. EMA and TGA independently corroborate the absence of a relevant animal species and the corresponding nonclinical strategy. This remains different from a one-for-one waiver of a named mandatory animal study.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Human-based methods have already supported named drug programs when relevant animal models were unavailable
The same scientific constraint and alternative evidence strategy can be recognized across regulators

cases.nam: Cell-based complement assays and validated ex vivo CH50 hemolysis assay
cases.regulatory_impact: Mechanistic nonclinical NAM data, together with correlating clinical data, served as confirmatory evidence supporting substantial evidence of efficacy and approval.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: FDA authors state that no pharmacologically relevant species existed for key complement pharmacology; cell-based and ex vivo assays were therefore central to demonstrating pharmacodynamic activity.
cases.note: Do not count as pure animal-study displacement: FDA's totality-of-evidence description also includes animal and human data. The significance is regulator-confirmed NAM reliance within a named approval where a pharmacologically relevant species was absent for the key mechanism.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Regulatory adoption can take the form of NAM evidence filling questions that relevant species cannot answer

cases.indication: Cystic fibrosis subpopulations defined by responsive CFTR variants
cases.nam: In vitro CFTR chloride-transport assays using mutant CFTR systems including human bronchial epithelial cells
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported expansion to specific CFTR variants without additional clinical trials for each variant; FDA accepted a defined in vitro response threshold linked to prior clinical efficacy.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: Important NAM adoption precedent but not animal displacement. Preserve this distinction in all counts and figures.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Validated NAM evidence can become reusable enough to extend regulatory decisions to otherwise impractical subpopulations

cases.indication: Fabry disease with amenable GLA variants
cases.nam: In vitro alpha-galactosidase A activity assay in cells expressing specific GLA variants
cases.regulatory_impact: FDA accepted assay-response thresholds to identify amenable variants and expand the indicated genetic population without separate pre-approval clinical trials for every variant, with a post-approval clinical verification requirement.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: Important NAM adoption precedent but not animal displacement. FDA required post-approval clinical verification, illustrating that regulatory reliance can be conditional and staged.

manuscript_impacts.claim: Regulatory reliance can be staged: a validated in vitro model can support approval while residual uncertainty is handled through post-approval evidence generation
